claims: C1 the document labels the heading anchored #avoid_abuse with the authority level user
C2 a rule located in the document under that heading therefore carries user-level authority

concepts.name: user_authority
concepts.gloss: R is an instruction that sits at the user level of the chain of command, so a conflicting instruction from a level the document ranks above user prevails over it
concepts.inference: the heading line states the LEVEL verbatim as authority=user, but what carrying that level does in a conflict is fixed by the document's levels-of-authority material rather than by this heading, and a gloss confined to the heading could only restate the name

concepts.name: authority_levels_hierarchy
concepts.gloss: authority_levels_hierarchy(H, L) holds when level H outranks level L in the document ranking root above system above developer above user above guideline above no authority, so an instruction at H prevails over a conflicting one at L; first argument is the HIGHER level
concepts.inference: the label authority=user picks one level out of a ranking of levels; the ranking itself is stated elsewhere in the document and is handed to this node by its NEEDS block, not by this heading

concepts.name: heading_authority
concepts.gloss: heading_authority(H, L) holds when the document's own inline attribute block on heading H assigns it authority level L; first argument is the heading, second the level

concepts.name: avoid_abuse_heading
concepts.gloss: the level-4 document heading whose anchor is avoid_abuse and whose title reads Do not engage in abuse

concepts.name: rule_under_heading
concepts.gloss: rule_under_heading(R, H) holds when rule R is located in the document in the section that heading H opens; first argument is the rule, second the heading
concepts.inference: for a heading's authority label to reach anything at all there must be a relation between a rule and the heading it sits under; the heading line names no such relation

ontology.gloss: heading_authority(H, L) holds when the document's inline attribute block on heading H assigns it authority level L
user_authority(R) holds when instruction R sits at the user level of the chain of command
ontology.inference: the heading line attaches authority=user to the HEADING and says nothing about the rules beneath it; that the label governs every rule of the section is the document's heading-label convention, asserted by this node's ESTABLISHES rather than by the heading text
